notes: THE SMALLEST PAGE IN PHASE 4: FIVE TOP-LEVEL BANDS, TWO OF THEM BLOCKS. Walked in DOM
order — `.crumbs` (chrome), `.hero` (chrome), `#program` (template, unguarded, LEADING),
`#how-it-works` (block 1), `#faq` (block 2), `<FinalBand>` (chrome). Every band is a block
with exactly one row here, or deliberately-unguarded chrome/template copy. There is no
third outcome and both failure directions have cost this project time.
`#program` IS THE ONE CONTENT BAND THAT STAYS IN THE TEMPLATE, and the reason is its aside,
not its prose. `.story-grid` is a two-column copy-beside-card split, and the card is
`aside.reward-card` (index.astro:186-222): a `.reward-stack` of two `.reward-row` price
blocks with a `$`/`50` split numeral, a `.reward-plus` divider, a three-item `.reward-meta`
checklist and a `.reward-jump` anchor with an `.arrow-mini`. `pricing_tiers` draws plan
cards with name/price/features; `card_grid` draws prose cards; neither is this shape, and
`copy_plus_stats` puts stat numerals in a column, not a $50-plus-$50 stack. Minting a
layout for one aside on one page is how a content model rots, so the band stays template
markup on both sides of the switch.
THAT IS ORDER-SAFE ONLY BECAUSE `#program` LEADS. It sits ABOVE the first block, so the
block run starting at `#how-it-works` leaves it exactly where it was. Put a block before it
and this becomes the LocalTrust fault — the band that came out at the bottom of the pilot
page because it was left out of the list. Its `sections[program]` row is therefore claimed
by no block, keeps feeding the template live, and is listed under `exempt.sections`. The
precedent is general-dentistry's `.closing`, which is the same decision at the other end of
the page.
NO RAIL. `tocLinks` comes back null from the live endpoint (verified 2026-08-29) and the
template draws no `.toc` nav at all, so `nav_label` resolves blank on both rows by the map
default and the template carries no derived-TOC loop. A loop feeding nothing would be
code that reads like a rail and is not one.
BAND VOCABULARY IS INVERTED ON THIS SHEET, as it is on every page in this family. `.dark`
is the LIGHT band — `.rp .section.dark { background: var(--vs-sage-pale) }`
(referral-program.css:95), and the sheet's own comment at :93-94 says so in as many words:
"Now a light band; text must read dark." `.alt` is the CHARCOAL one (:82). Every `band`
below is read off those rules, never off the class name. Reading the class would have put
charcoal on `#how-it-works`, which is the exact defect that let a word-level diff report
"0 of 48 differ" for days while 26 bands rendered the wrong colour.
EVERY LIVE ROW IS ACCOUNTED FOR, verified against https://1230613.us28.myftpupload.com/
graphql on 2026-08-29: 3 `sections` rows (program, how-it-works, faq), 3 `cards` rows (all
in group `steps`), 4 `faqs` rows, 1 `images` row (heroPrimary), `processSteps` null,
`tocLinks` null. Two rows are claimed by blocks, two are exempt with a reason.
THIS ROUTE MUST NOT BE BACK-FILLED BEFORE THE TWO COMPONENT CHANGES IT DEPENDS ON. Both
are named in `blocked_on` below. The `sub_foot` one is not cosmetic: ProcessStepsBlock
renders that field as `{subFoot}` today, which would print this route's anchor tag as
visible source text on a live client page.
blocked_on: 1. cms/mu-plugins/vs-content-model.php MUST BE ON THE CMS HOST BEFORE THE NEXT BUILD.
The manifest now names fields the un-deployed host does not have, and the capability
probe (vivid-smiles-website/src/loaders/pages.ts:191-266) throws for ALL 48 routes when
it finds them missing. This is the project's standing PHP-before-manifest order; it is
armed now and it is not this route's to close.
This route's `sub_foot` carries an anchor, so as written the band would print
`<a class="vs-link" href="{phone_href}">…` as TEXT. The component owner's change — render
it with `set:html` and pass it through the new src/blocks/site-tokens.ts `fillSiteTokens`
— must land first. As of this map being written, src/blocks/site-tokens.ts does not exist
in the working tree. A field declared, selected and read by nothing is this project's #1
failure, four times over; this is the mirror of it and it is why the literal is written
with tokens rather than with a `tel:` URL.
3. src/blocks/FaqBlock.astro must carry the `.answer` paragraph metrics before this route's
FAQ band ships — see `known_gaps` on the `faq` block. Not a blocker for correctness, a
blocker for the four answers reading at the size they read at today.

blocks.band_evidence: referral-program/index.astro:228 <section class="section dark"> — referral-program.css:95 — .rp .section.dark { background: var(--vs-sage-pale); color: var(--vs-ink) }. The sheet's comment at :93-94 names the inversion: this class is the LIGHT band on this page. ProcessStepsBlock maps sage-pale -> class `dark` (BAND_CLASS), so the emitted section class string is unchanged, and its `eyebrowLight` derivation (ProcessStepsBlock.astro:214) is true for sage-pale — which is what reproduces `class="eyebrow light"` at index.astro:231 without a field for it.
blocks.layout_evidence: `.rp .process-grid` is `repeat(3, 1fr)` (referral-program.css:364-367) wrapping `.process-card` > `.step-tag` + `.num` + h3 + p (index.astro:238-243). That is the `grid` shape at three columns, and THE LABEL COMES FIRST — which is the whole reason the shape is stated here rather than inferred. ProcessStepsBlock's `card` shape prints `.pstep-lbl` LAST; mapping this band as `card` would move the label to the bottom of three live step cards while leaving every word on the page, and a word-level diff cannot see that.

eyebrow.from_template: referral-program/index.astro:231. NOT moved: `sections[how-it-works].eyebrow` is null on the live endpoint, so the words exist only in the template. Transcribed, not authored.

sub_foot.literal: Referral cards are available at the front desk — call us at {phone} to grab a few on your next visit.
sub_foot.from_template: referral-program/index.astro:247-251, the `.process-foot` paragraph. Written as ONE string with the anchor inline. The template builds it from three JSX pieces separated by newlines-and-indent, which Astro emits as text nodes and compressHTML collapses to single spaces — so the rendered sentence has exactly one space before ``, and this literal has exactly that. Splicing it as separate expressions is how "Parker, CO80134" shipped on three pages.
sub_foot.token_note: `{phone_href}` and `{phone}` are resolved by src/blocks/site-tokens.ts at render, from src/data/contact.ts. A `tel:` URL stored here would be the practice's phone number with a second home, which is what the href policy forbids; unknown tokens pass through untouched, per AreaBand's rule.

blocks.cta_text_note: Left unset deliberately. `cta_text` draws the `.inline-cta` plate with a Book Online and a Call button beside the sentence, and this band has never had buttons. `sub_foot` is the bare-paragraph field and is the one this band needs (vs-content-model.php field_vs_blk_steps_sub_foot, whose own comment draws the same distinction).

steps.note: ALL 3 CMS ROWS MOVED, with the three template labels zipped onto them positionally. The page has a `cards` group named `steps` whose meta/title/body are word-for-word the hardcoded `steps` array at index.astro:22-41 — verified row by row against the live endpoint on 2026-08-29 — so the words move rather than being re-typed. `tag` is the one sub-field the CMS has nowhere to hold: "Step One/Two/Three" lives only in the template, so it is transcribed and zipped. Three literals against three cards; the backfill refuses a length mismatch.
steps.num_note: `num` comes from the card's `meta` ("01", "02", "03"), NOT from `@index2`. That derivation exists for the legacy `process_steps` repeater, which has no `num` sub-field; this page's numbers are real stored values and moving them is what keeps them the numbers the page prints.

known_gaps: `.process-foot` BECOMES `.process-outro`, AND THE TWO RULES DISAGREE. The page sheet
(referral-program.css:400-407) sets 14px/1.65; the block's scoped `.process-outro`
(ProcessStepsBlock.astro:1139-1146) sets 15.5px/1.7. `max-width: 60ch`, `margin: 40px auto
0` and `text-align: center` are identical in both. The class name changes, so the page rule
stops matching entirely — there is no cascade contest, the block's metrics simply apply.
Reconciling the two is the component owner's call and is named in `blocked_on` 2.
THE INLINE LINK KEEPS ITS COLOUR. `.rp .section.dark .vs-link { color: var(--sage) }`
(referral-program.css:408-410) is (0,3,0) and still matches: the block's `<section
class="section dark">` renders INSIDE `div.rp`. It has to be the page sheet that does this,
because `set:html` content carries no scope attribute, so no scoped rule in the component
can reach that anchor at all.
`.section-head center` LOSES ITS `center` TOKEN. The template writes `<div class="section-
head center">` (index.astro:230); the block emits `<div class="section-head">` and centres
unconditionally in its own scoped rule (ProcessStepsBlock.astro:507-511, `margin: 0 auto
64px; text-align: center`). Centring is preserved; the measure is not — `.rp .section-head`
is `max-width: 60ch; margin: 0 0 56px` (referral-program.css:104-107) against the block's
760px/64px. This is the same one-token loss every migrated route in the family already
carries, and it is block-owned.
THE EYEBROW GAINS TWO 28px RULES. `.rp .section-head .eyebrow` is `display: inline-block`
(referral-program.css:112) at (0,3,0); the block's scoped `.section-head .eyebrow` compiles
to (0,4,0) and wins, adding `inline-flex` plus the `::before`/`::after` hairlines
(ProcessStepsBlock.astro:512-523). Inherited from the block library, identical on all
fifteen migrated routes, recorded here rather than discovered later.
THE MOBILE STEP DIFFERS, THE DESKTOP DOES NOT. `.rp .process-grid` collapses 3 -> 1 at
991px (referral-program.css:473). The block collapses `.cols-3` to 2 at 991px
(ProcessStepsBlock.astro:1200-1209) and to 1 at 780px (:1219-1230), and its compound is
(0,3,0) against the page rule's (0,2,0), so the block wins inside the page's own media
query. Three cards therefore draw 2+1 between 780px and 991px where they draw 1+1+1 today.
Block-owned and shared with every other grid band in the library.
A SPECIFICITY TIE EXISTS ON `.process-card` AND IS INHERITED, NOT NEW. `.rp .process-card`
(referral-program.css:369) is (0,2,0); the block's scoped `.process-card` compiles to
`.process-card[data-astro-cid-…]`, also (0,2,0), and bundle order decides. That is the tie
the house rule says never to BUILD on — this map builds nothing on it. The identical tie
already ships on the ten back-filled routes whose sheets carry the same rule
(clear-aligners.css:369, teeth-whitening.css:351 and eight more), all of which measure
lossless, so the condition is settled in practice and is recorded here so nobody rediscovers
it as a defect of this route.

blocks.cta_note: NO CTA ROW. The template's FAQ band ends at `.faq-list` (index.astro:263-273) — there is no `.cta-row`, no button pair, nothing after the list. `cta_label` blank means FaqBlock's `hasCta` is false and the whole row is unemitted, which is the byte-identical outcome. Writing a label here would put two buttons on a band that has never had them.
blocks.cta_phone_first_note: Not set, and not needed: it only reorders the pair inside a `.cta-row` this band does not draw. Recorded because the field is new in this wave and a reviewer will look for it.

items.note: ALL 4 ROWS, IN ORDER, MOVED — including `open`, which is true on the first row only, verified live on 2026-08-29. `open` matters: the template writes `open={f.open}` (index.astro:267) and FaqBlock writes `open={f.open ?? false}`, so the first `<details>` renders expanded on both sides.

structured_data_note: THE FAQPage JSON-LD NOW READS THE BLOCK, NOT THE LEGACY REPEATER.
referral-program/index.astro derives `faqEntities` from the rendered source: the `items` of
the `PageFieldsBlocksFaqLayout` row when `hasBlocks`, the `faqs` repeater otherwise.
Structured data lives on the page and not in the band, so left alone it would keep
describing the pre-migration content the moment an editor edited the block's rows — a rich
result that disagrees with the page it is attached to. The two sources are identical the day
this runs, because the block's items are MOVED from that same repeater; the false branch
serialises byte-for-byte what it always has, which is what the byte-identity check below
verification: TEMPLATE ELSE-BRANCH PROVEN BYTE-IDENTICAL TO HEAD. Both files compiled with
@astrojs/compiler 3.0.1 `transform`; the emitted render bodies differ at exactly four sites
— the two guard wrappers, and `faqs.map` -> `faqEntities.map` in the FAQPage script. Every
surrounding static chunk, INCLUDING the newline-and-indent text nodes between bands, is
byte-identical. Separately, reverse-substituting the guards out of the new source yields a
file that diffs empty against `git show HEAD:` of it.
